# Data card

**Everything used in the evaluation is SYNTHETIC and generated by `data/generate.py` (seed 4016).** The instructor's GigSim, persona corpora and dev sets were *not* included in the starter kit I received (the zip contained a scaffold only), so I built stand-ins. Replace `data/personas/`, `gigsim/` and `evals/datasets/` with the official ones and re-run `make eval`; no code changes are needed beyond the adapter field mapping noted in `gigsim/README.md`.

| Asset | What | Real or synthetic |
|---|---|---|
| Personas (ml / web / data) | profile + ~18-22 projects each; per project a case study, README, client review (same project described three ways); one CV; 150 past proposals with outcomes (won 12% / replied 23% / ignored 65%) | synthetic (templated from a 48-skill vocabulary; ~40% of a project's skills are only *implied*, never named) |
| Marketplace jobs | 1,580 jobs (500/persona + 6% reposted duplicates): good, weak-fit, scam (unpaid work, off-platform contact/payment, guarantee bait), planted prompt-injection | synthetic |
| Dev sets | 200 jobs/persona with gold: bid/skip, scam flags, injection, relevant projects, fair price band | synthetic; gold derived from the generator, see limitations |
| Clients | 60 clients with histories + hidden preferences (dislike generic openings, budget ceiling) | synthetic |
| Kaggle Upwork datasets | listed in the assignment | **not used** (no download performed); documenting this rather than implying use. They would be the right source to calibrate price bands/categories. |

## Preprocessing
None beyond generation. Chunking for V0: 300-char windows, 60 overlap. Metadata on every chunk: persona, type, project, skills, date, industry, outcome (proposals).

## Limitations (read before trusting any number)
1. **Gold labels come from the same generator as the data.** "Relevant evidence" = projects whose explicit or implied skills overlap the job's requirements; "bid" = >= 60% of requirements covered by the persona. A system that learns the generator's logic scores high. Absolute numbers (e.g. bid/skip F1 ~0.98) are optimistic; relative comparisons are more meaningful.
2. Requirement extraction in retrieval evals is rule-based (regex on "experience with X"), which matches how synthetic jobs are written. Real posts are messier.
3. The simulated client (`gigsim_local/app.py::_decide`) is a rule-based model that rewards naming required skills, penalises generic phrases and over-budget bids. It is not an LLM client and not a real market; reply rates measure relative effects inside this simulator only.
4. `fit_support_relevance` (-3.0) was set by inspecting score separation over the persona skill lists, i.e. dev-adjacent.
5. Persona corpora are shared per persona; user-uploaded items are appended per persona (not per user), a tenancy limitation.
6. No licensing issues: all data is generated; no personal data. Prices in `agent/config.yaml` are placeholders for cost accounting.
